newsitem.title: USA: Thomaston Mills looking to turn profits.
newsitem.headline: Thomaston Mills looking to turn profits.

text.p: Thomaston Mills Inc said Tuesday that denim demand has softened, open end yarn prices are under pressure and that it is in the process of trying to reinstate profits.
President and Chief Executive Neil Hightower said in a statement that imports "have drastically impacted the lower thread count muslin business," which has been one of its mainstays.

For the third quarter ended March 29, the company reported a net loss of $1.86 million, or $0.28 per share, on sales of $70.73 million. In the prior year's third quarter, the company reported a net loss of $592,000, or $0.09 per share, on sales of $66.15 million.
Thomaston Mills said dye range project continues on schedule, and that the timing appears to be "quite good" since demand for piece dyed fabrics and dyed career apparel fabrics is improving.
